decisions.rationale: Lead the sun core for immediate Chlorophyll speed control and pressure on Rotom-Wash, Garchomp, and Aegislash. Kingambit and Aqua Tauros give two strong Fairy answers for Mega Floette while retaining physical cleanup and Intimidate.
decisions.notebook: Bring Charizard/Venusaur aggressively when the opposing Fire/Flying pressure can be contained; Mega Charizard Y enables instant sun and Chlorophyll Venusaur. Keep Kingambit and Aqua Tauros as primary Mega Floette punishers. Venusaur is key into Rotom-Wash and Garchomp; preserve its Focus Sash when possible. Talonflame can establish priority Tailwind while healthy and threatens Venusaur, so account for it in lead and turn-one planning. Aegislash has Wide Guard and Focus Sash, making single-target pressure or Sleep Powder valuable over blindly relying on Heat Wave.

decisions.rationale: Talonflame+Aegislash lead shuts down sun core: Wide Guard blocks Heat Wave/Sludge Bomb spread moves, Talonflame 0.25x resists Solar Beam, Aegislash immune to Poison. decisions.notebook: Opponent runs Charizard-Mega-Y sun core with Chlorophyll Venusaur, Kingambit, Raichu, Paldean Tauros, Sableye. Raichu Lightning Rod redirects Electric—avoid Rotom Thunderbolt into it. Game 2 plan: expect Sableye/Kingambit adjustments; Floette+Rotom-Wash or Floette+Garchomp may be stronger if they drop sun for Sableye lead.

decisions.rationale: Mega Evolve to establish sun and Chlorophyll immediately; Sleep Powder Talonflame to remove its repeated Life Orb Flying pressure after any priority Tailwind. Heat Wave punishes an aggressive Aegislash line and retains upside if it declines Wide Guard.
decisions.notebook: Opponent revealed: Life Orb Gale Wings Talonflame (Tailwind, Flare Blitz, Brave Bird, Quick Guard); Focus Sash Stance Change Aegislash (Wide Guard, Close Combat, Shadow Sneak, King’s Shield). Aegislash’s Wide Guard makes Heat Wave unreliable until it is slept or forced into another action; prioritize targeted sleep and preserve Venusaur’s Sash where feasible. Kingambit and Aqua Tauros remain primary answers to Mega Floette.

selection: Wide Guard (your side, including ally Talonflame)

Wide Guard at +3 priority beats Heat Wave, which in sun deals 97.8-140% to Aegislash and can OHKO through the sash slot. This blunts the sun core's opening while preserving both Pokemon.

decisions.rationale: Venusaur outspeeds both under sun and can deny Aegislash’s Wide Guard/King’s Shield pressure with Sleep Powder. Air Slash is Charizard’s strongest targeted option into the weakened Talonflame and can KO it, while avoiding Wide Guard entirely.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Sun enables immediate Solar Beam. Preserve Kingambit and Aqua Tauros where possible for Floette-Eternal; Kingambit is particularly valuable into Fairy once opposing Steel/Ghost pressure is removed. decisions.notebook: Opp team: Charizard-Y (Timid Drought), Venusaur (Modest Chlorophyll, Sash broken), Tauros-Aqua (Jolly Intimidate Expert Belt, burned), Kingambit (Adamant Defiant LO), Raichu (Timid Lightning Rod Sitrus), Sableye (Careful Prankster Mental Herb). Key: Spiritomb immune Fighting+Prankster; Aegislash immune Fighting. Wide Guard blocks Heat Wave/Rock Slide. King's Shield punishes contact. Foul Play uses target's Atk—strong vs high-Atk targets, weak vs Timid Charizard but still KOs at ≤24% (24.9-59.5% confirmed). Air Slash KOs Spiritomb at ≤36% (36.9-52.2%); Heat Wave KOs at ≤34% (35-49.7% spread). Consecutive Protect has reduced success rate (~1/3). Aegislash sleep duration 1-3 turns; ~1/3 wake chance per turn. Foul Play always KOs Venusaur at 1%. Game 2: expect Sableye/Kingambit or Raichu lead; Spiritomb strong vs both. Avoid Electric into Lightning Rod. Watch Sleep Powder, Sucker Punch, Intimidate stacking. Protect success resets on switch.

decisions.rationale: Heat Wave is the only Charizard attack that can force Aegislash to its Focus Sash; Venusaur’s faster-in-sun Solar Beam then removes it if Heat Wave lands and Wide Guard is unavailable. This converts the sleeping Aegislash immediately rather than preserving Charizard at 17%.
decisions.notebook: Aegislash is Focus Sash, Stance Change, with Wide Guard/Close Combat/Shadow Sneak/King’s Shield; it has strongly favored Wide Guard. Heat Wave from Mega Charizard Y in sun is a guaranteed OHKO through bulk but Sash leaves it at 1 HP; pair it with single-target follow-up where possible. Aegislash can use priority Shadow Sneak and threatens Kingambit with Close Combat. Spiritomb was Leftovers Pressure with Foul Play/Will-O-Wisp/Pain Split/Protect. Preserve Kingambit for Floette when feasible; Tauros is burned, so its physical output is reduced.

decisions.rationale: Spiritomb fainted and all bench Pokémon (Talonflame, Garchomp) are also fainted. Only Aegislash remains active with no replacement available for Spiritomb's slot. Game is lost—no legal continuation exists. Forfeiting. Aegislash is asleep anyway, so King's Shield is a moot selection.
decisions.notebook: Opp team: Charizard-Y (Timid Drought), Venusaur (Modest Chlorophyll, Sash broken), Tauros-Aqua (Jolly Intimidate Expert Belt, burned), Kingambit (Adamant Defiant LO), Raichu (Timid Lightning Rod Sitrus), Sableye (Careful Prankster Mental Herb). Key immunities: Spiritomb immune Fighting+Prankster; Aegislash immune Fighting/Poison. Wide Guard blocks Heat Wave/Rock Slide. King's Shield punishes contact. Foul Play uses target Atk—strong vs high-Atk targets. Game 1 lost: sun core (Charizard+Venusaur) overwhelmed; Aegislash slept by Sleep Powder was fatal. Game 2 plan: Expect Sableye/Kingambit or Raichu lead. Spiritomb strong vs both. Avoid Electric into Lightning Rod. Watch Sleep Powder, Sucker Punch, Intimidate stacking. Protect success resets on switch. Consecutive Protect ~1/3 success. Aegislash sleep 1-3 turns. Prioritize removing Venusaur early to deny Sleep Powder. Keep Aegislash away from Sleep Powder range. Consider leading Spiritomb+Talonflame or Spiritomb+Garchomp for better sun matchup. Talonflame Tailwind crucial for speed control vs Chlorophyll. Garchomp EQ hits Charizard hard but must watch Air Slash flinch.

reflections.summary: Won by using Mega Charizard Y’s single-target pressure to outlast Spiritomb’s Protect/Pain Split cycle, then putting the repeatedly Wide Guarding Aegislash to sleep. The Charizard Y/Venusaur core and Mega choice matched this four well.
reflections.adjustment: Keep Mega Charizard Y, but prioritize an earlier Venusaur Sleep Powder into Aegislash when it begins repeatedly using Wide Guard, allowing Charizard to attack without being constrained and reducing the opponent’s defensive stalling.
reflections.notebook: Aegislash is Focus Sash, Stance Change, with Wide Guard/Close Combat/Shadow Sneak/King’s Shield; it strongly favored repeated Wide Guard and can threaten Kingambit with Close Combat. Spiritomb is Leftovers Pressure with Foul Play/Will-O-Wisp/Pain Split/Protect and can prolong games through Protect plus Pain Split. Talonflame is Life Orb Gale Wings with Tailwind, Flare Blitz, Brave Bird, and Quick Guard. Garchomp is Lum Berry Rough Skin with Rock Slide/Earthquake/Scale Shot/Protect. Against this defensive Aegislash/Spiritomb structure, use Venusaur sleep pressure to disable Wide Guard and have Mega Charizard Y prioritize single-target attacks; preserve Kingambit for Floette if it is brought.

reflections.summary: Lost because the preview plan was poorly matched to Charizard-Y sun: our non-Mega four let opponent Charizard Mega-Y set sun and pressure with Air Slash/Solar Beam, while Venusaur's Sleep Powder removed Aegislash, leaving Spiritomb without support.
reflections.adjustment: Next game, do not lead or expose Aegislash into Venusaur; lead Spiritomb+Talonflame, use Tailwind immediately, focus Venusaur first, and keep Aegislash for later only after the sleep threat is gone; use Protect/Wide Guard to navigate Charizard attacks.
reflections.notebook: Opp primary win condition is Charizard-Y sun with Venusaur Chlorophyll; Venusaur repeatedly uses Sleep Powder and can survive one hit via Focus Sash. Charizard-Y favors Air Slash flinch and Solar Beam in sun. Tauros-Aqua provides Intimidate and Iron Head pressure even when burned. Expect Protect chaining, Sucker Punch from Kingambit, Fake Out/Nuzzle from Raichu, and Prankster disruption from Sableye. Our no-Mega plan must use Tailwind to contest Chlorophyll, remove Venusaur before sleep, keep Aegislash away from Sleep Powder, use Spiritomb Foul Play against Charizard/high-Attack targets, and reserve Wide Guard for spread moves like Heat Wave/Rock Slide.
